summary: H.R. 9795, the Never Forget the Victims of Terrorism: Joseph D. Mistrulli and Alan Kleinberg USVSST Fund Solvency Act, amends the Justice for United States Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Act. It directs the Secretary of the Treasury to make mandatory annual loans of $3 billion to the United States Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund for fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029, and requires these borrowed amounts to be distributed as part of the Fund's annual payments.

affected_groups.effect: Must loan $3 billion annually to the Fund for fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029, determine interest rates, and handle post-termination repayments.
Receive the fully distributed borrowed amounts as part of the required annual payment for fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029.
affected_groups.group: Recipients of the United States Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund annual payments

key_provisions: The Secretary of the Treasury must loan $3,000,000,000 to the Fund for each of the fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029, deposited within 30 days of each fiscal year's start.
The full borrowed amount for each fiscal year must be included and distributed as part of the Fund's required annual payment.
Borrowed amounts cannot be reserved, retained, or carried forward for any payment other than the required annual payment.
Borrowed amounts are available without further appropriation and bear interest based on the average market yield of comparable Treasury obligations.
Upon Fund termination, borrowed amounts and interest are repaid solely from post-expiration criminal and civil fines, penalties, and forfeitures involving a state sponsor of terrorism.
Borrowed amounts are treated as direct spending authority and not as new appropriations.
The borrowing authority sunsets on September 30, 2029, though previously borrowed amounts remain available until expended and subject to repayment.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the exact total size of the Fund prior to these loans.
The source text does not name the specific individuals who will receive the annual payments beyond those covered by the existing Fund criteria.
The source text does not specify the exact interest rate formula, only that it is determined by the Secretary of the Treasury based on comparable Treasury obligations.

It directs the Secretary of the Treasury to make mandatory annual loans of $3 billion to the United States Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund for fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029, and requires these borrowed amounts to be distributed as part of the Fund's annual payments.
summary_detail.significance: The bill injects $9 billion total ($3 billion per year) in mandatory borrowing into the United States Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund across fiscal years 2027, 2029, and 2029, altering the financial flow and distribution mechanics of the Fund.
